what_it_does: This paper addresses a scaling challenge in high-resolution mobile displays: adding more output channels to drive individual pixels requires more silicon area and increases cost. Conventional techniques for interpolating between voltage levels (to achieve fine color control) use circuits that either have inherent nonlinearity (making colors inaccurate) or require many capacitors and high-voltage transistors that consume chip area. The paper proposes a compact source driver that uses delta-sigma pulse-width-modulation (a digital technique that represents analog values as rapid on-off pulses) to replace the analog interpolation circuits. This approach reduces the number of capacitors and transistors needed per display channel while maintaining color accuracy, achieving extremely compact channel size (1884 square micrometers per channel).
